g.text: A compact, editorial overview: geography • economy • people • places to visit
Island nation • East Asia • Pacific Rim

text.tspan: Japan is an archipelago stretching from
Hokkaidō to Okinawa, shaped by volcanoes,
mountains, and a long coastline. Its culture
balances deep tradition with world-leading
design, technology, and craft.
Note: City points and outline are illustrative (not to scale).
Despite its dense cities, much of Japan is mountainous and forested. Seasonal change is a major theme—
from spring blossoms to autumn colors—while rail networks connect urban hubs to hot-spring towns,
coastlines, and alpine villages. Earthquakes and volcanic activity shape infrastructure, architecture,
and preparedness across the country.

g.text: Context for the GDP series shown on the right

text.tspan: Japan is a high-income economy with globally
competitive manufacturing, services, and
research-driven industries. Key themes include
an ageing population, productivity upgrades,
energy import dependence, and export strength
in vehicles, machinery, and electronics.

g.text: Currency fluctuations can affect nominal (US$) GDP.
Trends reflect both real output and exchange rates.

text.tspan: All values in trillion current US$

text.tspan: Tip: Consider rail passes and regional flights
to link far-apart highlights efficiently.

g.text: Selections combine city life, heritage, nature, and regional variety.
